Transport & itineraries · Ellora Cave 16

Ellora Caves One-Day Itinerary

A full day is the right scale for the ensemble: Buddhist worship halls, the great monolithic temple of Cave 16, other Brahmanical caves and the Jain group.

Google Maps ↗ ASI source listing ↗

Independent guide · Page reviewed 9 November 2026 · ASI listing consulted 2026-10-29

Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) is one monument within the UNESCO-listed Ellora Caves. Prices, opening status and routes are dated listings to re-check, not live confirmations.

The logic of the day

UNESCO describes 34 caves associated with Buddhist, Brahmanical and Jain traditions. A sensible day samples each tradition rather than attempting every cave: the point is to see how different communities used the same basalt scarp in different ways.

ASI suggests a 3–4 hour visit can prioritise Caves 10, 16, 21, 32 and 34. A full day adds time for slower looking, rests, the internal walking and the unexpected closure.

A possible shape

Begin with the daylight window in mind, since ASI lists sunrise-to-sunset visiting and a weekly Tuesday closure. Put the most important stop, Cave 16, early enough that a later closure or a tired group cannot crowd it out.

Confirm which caves are open before fixing the order, and drop stops freely. A list is a planning device, not a promise of access.

No fixed hours are guaranteed for the whole ensemble; reviewed 9 November 2026.

Beyond the property

Grishneshwar Temple, Daulatabad Fort and Bibi Ka Maqbara are separate destinations with their own admission, timings and travel. Adding any of them requires independent checks; they should not be assumed to be walking distance or to fit easily into the same day.

Suggested order

  1. Confirm opening status, weekly closure and current cave access
  2. Buddhist group: Vishvakarma Cave (Cave 10)
  3. Kailasa Temple (Cave 16): courtyard, facades and sculpture
  4. Brahmanical caves such as Cave 15, Cave 21 or Dumar Lena (Cave 29)
  5. Jain group: Indra Sabha (Cave 32)
  6. Return to the agreed pick-up point; optional separate regional stop

An order of attention, not a timed guarantee. Closed areas, conservation work and your own pace take priority.

Frequently asked questions

Can I see all 34 caves in one day?

That is not a realistic promise. Closed areas, the length of the scarp and the time Cave 16 deserves all argue for a representative selection.

Which caves should not be missed?

ASI suggests Caves 10, 16, 21, 32 and 34 as priorities for a shorter visit. Cave 16 is the focus of this site.

Can I add Daulatabad Fort the same day?

It is a separate destination with its own travel and admission. Check both independently and do not assume an easy combination.
